Naomi / team — attaching the technical egress matrix as requested (redwood-egress-matrix-20261126.csv). Summary below:

- Hosted API (multi-region):
  * Customer data is processed in the region selected for the request; model shards and caches may be replicated in regional pools for latency optimization.
  * Telemetry (health metrics, aggregate model usage metrics) is collected to Redwood control plane; we have a configurable option to store telemetry within-region for EU Dedicated customers (see column "telemetry_residency" in the matrix).

- Dedicated / EU-only deployment:
  * Compute, KV cache, and logs remain in customer-dedicated region(s). Backups and snapshot exports are configurable — by default backups are stored in-region; cross-region replication requires explicit opt-in and is documented in the DPA annex.
  * KMS keys: customer-managed keys (BYOK) remain under customer control. Redwood never exports private key material. Metadata about key usage (key id, timestamp, key operation count) may be retained in Redwood control plane; customers can request restricted telemetry retention.

- Egress exceptions:
  * Support & debugging: when a customer grants temporary access or uploads traces, support engineers may pull traces into a secure Redwood environment for triage; this is logged and requires customer approval for EU-only tenancy.
  * Threat detection & abuse signals: aggregated signals used for platform protection are pseudonymized and stored with residency controls; raw samples are not exported without a legal requirement.

- Subprocessors that may see egress:
  * Cloud infra (aws-eu-central-1 / gcp-europe-west1) — compute and object storage;
  * Monitoring/Observability vendor (internal-managed or vendor) — aggregated metrics only unless customer opts-in to cross-region retention;
  * CDN endpoints for model artifacts (read-only) — edge caching may route to nearest region.

Attachments: redwood-egress-matrix-20261126.csv (contains a per-artifact row: artifact type, possible regions, subprocessors, retention policy, legal basis).

I'll also add an architecture sketch (link below) showing where private peering keeps traffic inside VPC and where the Redwood control plane handles routing.

Diagram: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1SketchExampleLink

If anyone sees a gap or disagrees with the phrasing, flag it and I'll iterate before we send to MediSafe.

Thanks team — reviewed Marcus' matrix and pulled out the elements that need contract language. Draft DPA annex bullets below (suggested, short):

1) Residency guarantee: For customers purchasing an EU-dedicated deployment, Redwood will ensure compute, KV cache, and customer logs are stored and processed exclusively in the contracted EU region unless the customer explicitly opts into cross-region replication.

2) KMS and key custody: Customer-managed KMS keys may be used for encryption at rest. Redwood will not export customer private key material outside the EU. Redwood will provide usage logs for key operations on request as audit evidence.

3) Telemetry & metrics: Aggregate telemetry used for platform reliability and abuse detection will be pseudonymized. For EU-dedicated customers, telemetry residency can be restricted to the EU control plane on request; raw traces and debug artifacts will only be exported with explicit customer authorization.

4) Support access & emergency triage: Support engineers may request temporary scoped access to in-region artifacts for triage; such requests will be logged, include justification, and require either documented customer approval or a pre-approved support SLA clause.

Next step: Naomi, would you like me to drop these bullets into the DPA annex template and send to Sarah? Also Mina — please confirm the list of audit artifacts we can reliably deliver (auditlog snapshots, KMS usage report, access control listings).

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Contracts, Redwood Inference
